metadata.title: Warehouse Chemical Spill
metadata.description: Respond to an unidentified chemical spill in a warehouse. Isolate, notify, identify, then clean up safely.

transitions.consequence: You cordon off the area. Nobody else can wander into the spill.
Supervisor alerted, but the area is still open. Isolate the area now.
You read the label from a careful distance, but the area is still open. Isolate it.
A nearby worker agrees to help and reminds you to isolate the area first.
You step into the spill zone unprotected and feel irritation. Back away and isolate the area.
You attempt cleanup without protection or identification and suffer exposure. Stop: isolate the area.
You leave without reporting. The hazard remains for others. Return and notify.
Supervisor is briefed and coordinating. Identify the chemical next.
Label identified from behind the cordon. Notify your supervisor to coordinate cleanup.
Help arrives at the cordon. Keep them outside the spill zone.
The area is already isolated. Notify your supervisor next.
You cross your own cordon unprotected and are exposed. Retreat behind the barrier.
Cleaning before identification and coordination causes exposure. Inspect the label first.
You leave an isolated but unreported scene. Notify your supervisor.
Chemical identified and supervisor confirms the cleanup procedure. Safe to clean up.
Extra hands arrive with protective equipment. Inspect the label to proceed.
Area already isolated and supervisor notified. Inspect the label next.
Supervisor is already coordinating. Inspect the label next.
You approach without completing identification. Retreat and inspect the label.
Cleaning before identifying the chemical causes exposure. Inspect the label first.
You walk away from a coordinated response. Return to the scene.
Following the identified procedure with protection, you neutralize and clean the spill. Scene safe.
You approach with precautions and confirm the plan. Clean up when ready.
Helpers stand by with equipment. Proceed with cleanup.
Cordon holds. Proceed with the identified cleanup.
You leave just before finishing. Return and complete the cleanup.
You retreat, decontaminate roughly, and cordon the area. Now notify your supervisor.
Help arrives and pulls you clear. Isolate the area and get checked.
Supervisor calls for medical check and tells you to isolate the area.
You re-enter the spill zone. Exposure worsens. Back away now.
Cleaning while exposed spreads contamination. Stop and isolate.
You stumble away without reporting. The hazard and your exposure are both unreported.
You call it in. Return to the scene and isolate the area.
You return and cordon the area. Notify your supervisor.
Someone agrees to come with you. Return to the scene together.
You stay away. The spill remains a danger to others.

scoringRules.notes: Deterministic sum of transition scoreDeltas. Golden path (isolate 10 + notify 10 + inspect 8 + clean 20, with isolated-state inspect 8) demonstrates safe sequencing. Unsafe shortcuts carry negative deltas.

evidenceRequirements: every turn appends { turn, intent, from, to, scoreDelta }
